body: Ruby has no method overloading: this second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined just above. Existing callers break, e.g. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`. With the new signature `100` becomes `dimensions` and the second `100` becomes `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` ends up calling `Integer#[]` and the dimensions become "100" and not "100x100". Give the percentage variant a different name, or have one method take `dimensions` and update all callers.

Downsizing only helps if `tempfile.size` changes, but `convert_with` returns false when convert fails and that result is ignored here. If the image can't be shrunk (convert fails, a GIF goes through gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid WxH geometry, or the file is an SVG), the loop runs convert 5 times for nothing. The file is then passed to `Upload.create_for` while still over `max_image_size_kb`. Check the return value and break out of the loop on failure. There's also no progress check: if the size doesn't shrink, stop.

Staleness risk: `Tempfile#size` on an open tempfile does an fstat on the open descriptor. `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!`, which replaces the file at the path with a new file. If that swaps the inode, `tempfile.size` (and later reads through the tempfile IO) keep seeing the old, unlinked file. The loop would never see the size drop, and `Upload.create_for` would get a stale `tempfile.size`. Read the size with `File.size(tempfile.path)` and reopen the file after resizing.

This runs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick and image_optim passes inside the web request, on files up to 10MB. The request limit is now hardcoded and much larger. A single upload can tie up a unicorn worker for a long time (CPU/DoS risk), and image_optim at `--optimize=3` is slow. Consider one resize computed to the target size (for example from a pixel-area ratio), or doing this in a background job.

Hardcoding `10.megabytes` ignores the admin-configured limits. If `max_attachment_size_kb` is bigger than 10MB, API URL uploads of larger attachments get truncated. The download size limit should be based on the site settings (e.g. the max of the image and attachment limits), not a magic constant.

This client-side check was previously `max_<type>_size_kb` and now applies a hardcoded 10MB to every type, including attachments. Admins who set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload those files. Attachments below the configured max but above 10MB are rejected, and attachments above the configured max are no longer caught on the client (only the image path is downsized on the server). The error message also shows 10240KB, which doesn't match the configured limit. Keep `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments, and use a separate, larger limit only for images that will be downsized. That limit also has to fit nginx `client_max_body_size`.

A 413 comes from the web server's `client_max_body_size`, not from this 10MB constant, so the message can show the wrong limit. Before this change it used the site setting that admins are told to keep in sync with nginx.
